title.narrative: Sustainable Reintegration of the survivor/trafficked Bangladeshi returnee migrant workers (SuRe)

description.narrative:
A total of 3.4 million Bangladeshis have migrated overseas for employment during 2018-2022, roughly 700,000 per year. The remittances sent by Bangladeshi migrant workers was nearly USD 20 billion per year during the last five years which plays a significant role to increase the country's foreign currency reserve having a trickle down effect on the overall economy of the country. Unfortunately, the government does not ensure fair and ethical recruitment system which put thousands of workers in trafficked situation in the migration cycle. Though the government maintains a database of the outgoing migrants, there is no system in place to record the information of the returnees. OKUP has provided direct assistance to the vulnerable returnees since 2010. Roughly 300 to 400 survivor returnees including the victims of trafficking have received direct assistance from OKUP annually.
Building upon a CAFOD project focusing on reintegration of returnee migrant workers, this project will provide co-funding to OKUP on a UNODC funded project supporting survivor women and girl returnee migrants who have been trafficked and abused. Areas of support include: trauma informed psycho-social support, access to safe houses, medical assistance, legal aid and entrepreneurship development training. CAFOD's contribution is toward a key element of the project: the 'Peer Counseling' model that was undertaken by OKUP in the previous projects which seeks to create a community-led support system for the survivor returnee migrant workers through capacity building and mentoring of peer counsellors.
